claims.claim: The default authentication choice for a tool is end-user credentials.
claims.quote: Authentication | Runs the tool with the user's credentials (End user, the default) or the maker's credentials (Maker-provided).

claims.claim: Makers can choose maker-provided authentication credentials for tools.
claims.quote: Maker-provided credentials: The tool uses your credentials. Use this method for shared resources, or when users shouldn't need their own access.

claims.quote: An end user might retrieve information or perform actions that only the maker's account is permitted to do.

claims.claim: Control maker credential options can remove makers' ability to select their credentials for tools.
claims.quote: You choose whether makers can select to use their own credentials for authenticating tool connections, to use the end-user's credentials, or to have access to both.

claims.claim: Preventing maker credentials immediately changes the tools to require end-user credentials.
claims.quote: The feature immediately turns off the maker's ability to select their credentials ... All tools for all agents in the impacted environments instantly change to require end-user credentials at runtime.

claims.claim: The maker-credential rule applies to existing and new agents in the affected environment.
claims.quote: Once active, all existing and new agents in that environment adhere to this rule
